concept.title: The Game
concept.subtitle: Black-and-white psychological horror
concept.short: Black-and-white horror game where you photograph paranormal events in a 1960s Irish pub. Sound is your main tool for finding anomalies.
concept.detailed: You have a Polaroid camera and 12 shots. Anomalies happen every 30-50 seconds. Glasses levitate, shadows move on their own, chairs spin. Audio cues tell you where to look: a glass clinks, footsteps echo from nowhere, a chair scrapes across the floor. Without sound, you're blind. Once you capture the evidence, arrange the photos on a corkboard in chronological order to piece together what's happening.
concept.desc:
You're trapped in a black-and-white 1960s Irish pub where reality is breaking down. Anomalies appear every 30 to 50 seconds, and sound is your only tool for finding them. Put on headphones and listen carefully. A glass clinks in the corner. Footsteps echo from an empty hallway. A chair scrapes across the floor by itself. Follow the audio to locate each disturbance, then photograph it. You have exactly 12 shots, so choose wisely.

The pub has constant supernatural activity. Glasses levitate off the bar. Shadows detach from their owners and move independently. Chairs spin on their own. The grainy black-and-white aesthetic makes everything feel like a forgotten photograph from decades ago.

Audio is the core mechanic. Mute the game and you can't find anomalies. You won't know where to look, what's happening, or how to survive. Every creak, whisper, and crash is information.

Once you've captured your evidence, race to the corkboard and arrange the photos in the correct chronological order. This is how you piece together what's happening and why. But work quickly. Something is hunting you through the pub, and time is running out.

gameplay.title: Core Mechanic: Observe → Capture → Connect
gameplay.observe_desc: Anomalies appear every 30-50 seconds. Environmental sounds guide you to their location.
gameplay.capture_desc: Use your Polaroid camera to photograph the anomaly. You have limited film, and every reload leaves you vulnerable.
gameplay.connect_desc: Arrange photos on the pin board in the correct order to reveal the truth and reach the good ending.

audio_systems.title: Audio Implementation
audio_systems.rtpc_desc: RTPC value (0-5) controls ambient layers in Wwise. More photos on the board = higher tension. Breathing gets heavier, ambient drones intensify. Smooth crossfades, no hard cuts.
audio_systems.switches_desc: Each room has its own ambient layers that crossfade as you move. Bathroom has spatialized toilet and faucet sounds. Footsteps change based on surface. Wood, tiles, concrete.
audio_systems.delegates_desc: Audio systems communicate through delegates. C++ handles game logic, Blueprint handles audio. Keeps everything modular. Change one without breaking the other.
audio_systems.spatial_desc: Full 3D positional audio for anomalies, enemy, and environmental cues. Spatial accuracy is required for gameplay. You can't find threats without it.

dev_tools.title: Development Tools
dev_tools.fixer_desc: Custom C++ plugin that restores Wwise integration after Perforce pulls. Runs automatically, no manual fixing needed.
dev_tools.rebuilder_desc: Deletes Intermediate and Saved folders, regenerates project files. Fixes linker errors that happen after bad merges.

anomalies.title: Anomaly Types
anomalies.desc: Semi-randomized disturbances that escalate as the game progresses.
anomalies.object_desc: Chairs rotate on their own, glasses levitate mid-air, and cutlery clatters without cause. Everyday objects begin to defy the laws of physics.
anomalies.env_desc: The space itself warps and distorts. Radio static erupts from nowhere, lights flicker erratically, and the clock accelerates its ticking.
anomalies.shadow_desc: Human silhouettes materialize in the darkness. Shadows peel away from their source objects and move independently. Motion occurs in places where no light source could cast it.

footstep.title: Footstep System: Surface Detection & Audio Routing
footstep.desc: Footsteps change based on what you're walking on. Wood, tiles, concrete. The system detects the surface and switches sounds in Wwise automatically.
footstep.what: C++ component does a line trace down from the player, checks the Physical Material, and maps it to a Wwise Switch (Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete).
footstep.how: Physical Material is detected using Unreal's surface system. That gets mapped to a Switch name. Blueprint Audio Manager gets the delegate and plays the right sound in Wwise.
footstep.why: C++ handles detection, Blueprint handles audio. I can add new surfaces without touching C++ code. Audio designer can change Switch names in Wwise without code changes.
footstep.result: Footsteps match every surface automatically. No manual work needed. Adding new materials is straightforward.

player_audio.title: Player Audio System: Delegate-Based Communication
player_audio.desc: Player actions trigger audio through delegates. Camera shot, zoom, photoboard interaction. Each action calls the right Wwise event.
player_audio.what: PlayerCharacter (C++) defines multicast delegates. When you take a photo or zoom, the delegate broadcasts. Blueprint Audio Manager listens and plays the sound.
player_audio.how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegates that work with Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint. Multicast means multiple listeners can react to one action.
player_audio.why: PlayerCharacter doesn't know anything about audio. Audio Manager doesn't know anything about player logic. I can test and change each independently.
player_audio.result: Adding new audio actions is easy. No hardcoded calls. Audio designers can change sounds in Wwise without touching player code.

rtpc.title: Dynamic Tension System: RTPC-Driven Ambience
rtpc.desc: More photos on the board = higher tension. Ambient intensity increases as you progress.
rtpc.what: RTPC value (0-5) controls ambient layers in Wwise. PhotoboardWidget tracks how many photos you've placed. More photos = higher RTPC value = more intense ambience.
rtpc.how: When you place a photo, UpdateAmbientRTPC() finds the AkAmbientSound actor (tagged 'AmbientProgressive') and sets the RTPC value. Wwise crossfades between ambient layers based on that value.
rtpc.why: RTPC gives smooth transitions between tension states. No audio jumps. I control crossfade curves in Wwise without touching code.
rtpc.result: Tension builds smoothly as you progress. Tweak curves in Wwise, atmosphere adapts automatically.

wwise_arch.title: Wwise Architecture: Switch Containers & Photoboard Integration
wwise_arch.desc: Switch Containers work with the RTPC system. More photos collected = different ambient layers activate.
wwise_arch.what: RTPC value (0-5 from photos) drives Switch Container selection in Wwise. Each Switch state has different ambient layers. RTPC handles smooth crossfades, Switch Containers handle structural changes.
wwise_arch.how: PhotoboardWidget sends RTPC value. Wwise uses that to pick the right Switch state and crossfade between layers.
wwise_arch.why: Switch Containers give discrete layer control. RTPC gives smooth transitions. Together: structural changes (different ambient sets) and intensity progression.
wwise_arch.result: Ambient responds to player progress. This is partial implementation. Full system will have more layers and complexity.

anomaly_audio.title: 3-Stage Anomaly Detection
anomaly_audio.description: Every anomaly triggers three audio layers:
anomaly_audio.alert: Alert (0.5s): Static burst marks the spawn
anomaly_audio.hint: Hint (1-2s): Directional sound points you there
anomaly_audio.conclusion: No visuals, no UI markers, just sound. Audio is the detection system.

challenges.title: Challenges & Solutions
challenges.desc: Problems encountered during development and how I addressed them.

challenge1.title: Workflow Optimization Tools
challenge1.problem: Multi-institutional student project had workflow problems. Wwise integration broke after Perforce pulls. Unreal compilation took too long, causing downtime.
challenge1.solution: Built Wwise Unreal Fixer and Unreal Engine Rebuilder. Wwise Fixer restores broken integration after Perforce pulls (one click). Rebuilder automates compilation to cut downtime. Made these to help the student team work faster.

code_explanations.footstep_what: Function detects surface type under player using line trace downward from player position.
code_explanations.footstep_how: Validates owner and world exist, then performs line trace using ECC_WorldStatic channel. Checks object's Physical Material and maps SurfaceType enum to Wwise Switch name (Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete).
code_explanations.footstep_why: Using Physical Material allows automatic detection without manually tagging each surface. The enum-to-Switch mapping is a one-time setup that connects Unreal's surface system to Wwise - this is configuration, not hardcoded audio calls. Audio designer can modify Switch names in Wwise without code changes.
code_explanations.delegate_what: Definition of multicast delegates for player actions that trigger audio events.
code_explanations.delegate_how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegate that can be broadcast from C++ and listened to in Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint.
code_explanations.delegate_why: Multicast delegates allow multiple listeners (e.g. Audio Manager) to react to one action. Dynamic delegates work with Blueprint, giving audio designer full control without modifying C++ code.
code_explanations.rtpc_what: Function updates RTPC value in Wwise based on number of photos placed on board.
code_explanations.rtpc_how: Validates world exists, then finds AkAmbientSound actor by tag 'AmbientProgressive' (more efficient and reliable than name string search). Sets RTPC value (0-5) corresponding to number of important photos. Wwise automatically crossfades between ambient layers.
code_explanations.rtpc_why: RTPC gives smooth transitions between tension states. I can control crossfade curves for each layer in Wwise, giving full control over emotional progression without code modifications.

enemy_presence.title: Enemy Presence Audio System
enemy_presence.desc: Enemy gets closer, audio gets worse. Two layers stack up: ambient dread (low drones, unsettling textures) and stressed character breathing. Both scale with proximity via RTPC.
enemy_presence.what: System tracks enemy distance and triggers audio layers. Closer enemy = more intense audio. Dread ambience and breathing stress scale with proximity.
enemy_presence.how: OnProximityChanged() receives proximity value (0-100%), starts/stops dread layers, updates RTPC for intensity, adjusts breathing stress. All validated with null safety checks.
enemy_presence.why: No hard cuts when the enemy moves. RTPC smooths the transitions. The breathing layer adds urgency without cluttering the mix.
enemy_presence.result: The closer the enemy, the worse everything sounds. Dread layers and stressed breathing stack up as it gets closer.

ambience_zones.title: Ambience Zone System
ambience_zones.desc: Location-based audio that changes as you move through different areas of the pub.
ambience_zones.what: 5 distinct zones with unique ambient soundscapes: Main Bar, Back Room, Bathroom, Hallway, Storage. Each has specific audio atmosphere.
ambience_zones.how: Trigger volumes detect player location. On zone enter, fade out previous ambience and fade in new zone's layers. Smooth crossfades prevent audio jumps.
ambience_zones.why: Each room sounds different. Bathroom: tiles + reverb. Bar: glasses + crowd murmur. You know where you are just by listening.
ambience_zones.result: Smooth transitions between zones. Each room sounds different, so you always know where you are in the pub.

anomaly_system.title: Anomaly Audio System
anomaly_system.desc: 3-stage detection system for 10 different paranormal anomaly types with unique audio signatures.
anomaly_system.what: 3 detection stages: Far (general alert), Medium (directional cue), Close (precise location). 10 anomaly types including Levitating Glass, Shadow Movement, Spinning Chair.
anomaly_system.how: Distance-based RTPC drives audio intensity. Directional audio guides player to anomaly. Each anomaly type has unique sound signature for identification.
anomaly_system.why: Sound is how you find anomalies. Alert signals the spawn, hint gives direction, presence confirms the location. Mute the game and you're blind.
anomaly_system.result: Sound is the only way to find anomalies. Each type has its own signature, so experienced players learn to identify them by ear.

project_metrics.title: Project Scale & Technical Metrics
project_metrics.desc: Production statistics and technical implementation scope.
project_metrics.what: Sprint 3/5 production phase. Multi-institutional collaboration. Extensive C++ and Blueprint implementation with Wwise integration.
project_metrics.how: 12+ C++ classes for audio systems, 8+ Blueprint audio managers, 200+ Wwise events/switches/RTPCs, 5 location zones, 10 anomaly types.
project_metrics.why: This is my biggest Wwise implementation so far. Had to learn how multiple audio systems can work together without triggering each other's bugs.
project_metrics.result: Designers can tweak values in Data Assets without waiting for code rebuilds. When something crashes, it's usually clear which system caused it.

achievements.opt: Reduced CPU usage by caching enemy distance calculations and using event-based updates
achievements.flicker: Implemented hysteresis thresholds for audio states to prevent rapid on/off toggling

challenges_list.c1_prob: Sounds would rapidly toggle on/off when player stood near trigger edges
challenges_list.c1_sol: Implemented hysteresis: separate start/stop thresholds (Start at 70%, Stop at 60%)
challenges_list.c2_prob: Calculating distance to all enemies every frame was too heavy
challenges_list.c2_sol: Added a caching system that updates the closest enemy reference periodically, not every frame
